full_judgment:
2. Facts, relevant for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that, one Md Nazrul Islam, as petitioner (plaintiff), had filed Pre-emption Miscellaneous Cise No.47 of 1983, on 10-5-1983, before the court of the then Munsif, Joypurhat, Bogura (now Senior Assistant Judge, Joypurhat), under the provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (SAT), 1950, against Md Majibur Rahman and others, seeking right of pre-emption in respect of the suit property mentioned in the schedule to the petition for pre-emption. The contention of the pre-emptor is that, he is the co-sharer by inheritance and the opposite parties No. 1-4 are strangers in the suit property and that the transfer deed No. 4932 dated 21-4-1983 was executed by pre-emptee No. 5 (seller) in favour of the pre-emptee opposite parties No. 1- 4 (purchasers), without their knowledge and, that, since he is co-sharer in the suit property, therefore, he is entitled to a decree for pre-emption as prayed for. 

 3. The opposite parties No. 1- 4 contested in the suit by filing written objection denying all material allegations made in the petition for pre-emption. They have also stated that, the pre-emptor is not a co-sharer in the suit property and that the suit was barred by limitation. It has also been asserted that, the sale of the property was negotiated in presence of the pre-emptor and the deed No. 4932 dated 21-4-1983 was executed with his knowledge, since he was not interested to purchase the same. It has further been stated that, the pre-emptees have developed the suit property and have been occupying the same since their purchase and that the necessary parties were not included in this case. Hence, this pre-emption case is liable to be dismissed. 

 14. In this case, the pre-emptees has specifically stated in their written objection and had testified that, the pre-emptor was aware about the sale from the very beginning and he was mediator. On this point, the pre-eemptor did not adduce any evidence as to how or from whom he got the knowledge of the impugned transfer. On the other hand, the question of limitation has been specifically pleaded in the written objection. Besides, section 3(3) of the Limitation Act, 1908, imposes a statutory duty on the court to frame and decide the issue of limitation, whether it has been pleaded or not by any of the parties of the proceeding. 

 19. Having read the judgment of the trial court, I do not find any discussion, nor finding that the pre-emptors are co-sharers of the CS recorded owners. Although, it has been recorded that, “দাখিলী সি,এস,এম,আর,আর খতিয়ান দৃষ্টে প্রমাণিত হয় যে, প্রার্থক নালিশী জোতে উত্তরাধিকারী সুন্রে শরীক।”But, there is no discussion in the judgment as to who are the CS and MRR recorded owners and how the pre-emptors are related to them. The court must arrive at specific findings clearly showing the basis and the accrual of the right of pre-emption, moreover, when the pre-emptee has specifically stated in their written objection that, the pre-emptor is not co-sharer in the suit property.
